author: TEDx Talks
description:
Ever searched your symptoms online and spiraled into worst-case scenarios within minutes? This engaging  talk reveals how to look up health concerns wisely, stay grounded, and use tools for clarity -- not fear. Dr. Whyte is a physician, public health advocate, and executive currently serving as the CEO of the American Medical Association. He is consistently recognized as a leading voice on health topics.  He has written five best-selling books, helping people take control of their health. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: How to Google your symptoms without freaking out | John Whyte | TEDxNashville

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this raw, deeply personal talk, DePrice Taylor unpacks how generational trauma teaches us to play roles instead of knowing who we are, and shares the hard-won journey walking away from relationships that denied her own identity.  It's a powerful reminder that self-discovery isn't selfish — it's the foundation for real connection. Because we can't connect to others until we know ourselves.

 DePrice Taylor is a civic leader, writer, and sports business professional focused on personal transformation, purposeful growth, the power of human connection, and expanding opportunities for others.

A native of Detroit, a city known for its grit, soul, and pride, DePrice carries that spirit with her. It shows up in how she lives her life, how she leads, and how she shows up for others—with intention, heart, and a commitment to community. Her journey is rooted in overcoming adversity, growing up in an environment shaped by trauma and chaos, yet finding her way forward with faith and determinat
title: Disconnection can be an act of love too | DePrice Taylor | TEDxKC

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this candid talk, behavioral scientist Dr. Michelle Rozen argues that the deepest threat AI poses isn't to our jobs, but to our sense of self, and that comforting claims like "AI can't replicate creativity" are quietly eroding trust. Her answer: what we think of as a technology crisis, is a soul crisis wearing a technology costume. Knowing what matters the most to us as individuals is what makes us unique as humans, and what no machine can ever do for us. 

 Dr. Michelle Rozen, Ph.D. is a behavioral scientist and published researcher who has dedicated her career to one of the most consequential questions of our time: why do human beings resist change, and what does science tell us it actually takes to lead through it?

Her groundbreaking studies on decision-making, goal execution, and AI adaptation have redefined how organizations approach change.

Her extensive research on goal execution where she found that only 6% of people follow through on their goals, became the foundation of
title: If AI can do what I do, who am I? | Michelle Rozen | TEDxKC

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this wildly original, funny talk, Jared Ficklin uses AI-generated Burning Man photos, a cosmic origin story, and a case for space elevators to make the argument for "technophilia" — a philosophy where technology amplifies humanity instead of replacing it, guided by love and intellect rather than raw capability. It's a vision for how we might finally take on humanity's largest, most intractable problems.

 Jared is a Frog Design Fellow & former founding partner of argodesign. He believes experience is key to design and has spent more than two decades finding value for the user in innovative technology and bringing solutions to large organizations. He is currently the Chief Product & Design Officer for the Collaborative Intelligence startup SynthBee.

He is also a futurist and an interactive artist creating or participating in large-scale social experiments from SXSW to Burning Man with a focus on the intersection of humanity and technology. He spoke at TED. He is a maker. He is the
title: Technophilia, AI, and space elevators: A love letter to the future | Jared Ficklin | TEDxKC

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Every birthday, Diana Kander doesn't just get older — she "upgrades." In this warm, funny, and unexpectedly moving talk, Diana shares her yearly ritual of becoming a new version of herself, from refining her stage presence to confronting the human tendency to default to the status quo. This is a story about immigration, motherhood, and the courage to choose who you were meant to be.

 When Diana Kander was just 8 years old, she and her family escaped the Soviet Union, entered the United States as refugees, and resettled in Kansas City without money or the ability to speak English. From these humble beginnings, Diana became a Georgetown-educated attorney, a university professor, the founder of 10 companies, a consultant to Fortune 500 companies and government leadership teams, and a New York Times bestselling author whose books have been taught in more than 100 universities and translated into many languages. And her parents would like you to know that her sister is a doctor. This talk
title: My year of becoming brave | Diana Kander | TEDxKC

author: TEDx Talks
description:
A communication researcher spent months in prison studying men who'd harmed their partners — and found not monsters, but people taught that winning, at any cost, was the meaning of being a man. Meggie Mapes traces how the "language of violence" is learned, and what it actually takes to change the rules of the game — in relationships, and in ourselves.

 Dr. Meggie Mapes is a communication researcher, educator, and author dedicated to empowering individuals and organizations to communicate with authenticity and impact. She is a professor and director at the University of Kansas, author of the award-winning open textbook Speak Out, Call In, editor of the Journal of Communication Pedagogy, and founder of the consulting firm Meggie Mapes, LLC. 

Her research takes her inside prisons, where Dr. Mapes has co-facilitated batterer intervention programs to study the cultural beliefs that reproduce gender violence. What she found — that violence is a meaning problem, not a monster problem — is
title: What prison taught me about gender violence | Meggie Mapes | TEDxKC

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Musicality, storytelling, and songwriting blend perfectly as Latin Grammy-nominated Making Movies takes the TEDxKC stage to perform three original songs: Ámame, Anabel and Lover. Experience the band's electric, genre-blending sound live.

 Making Movies is the Latin Grammy–nominated group led by Enrique Chi — born in Santiago, Panamá, and raised in the American Midwest — forging a sound guided by tradition, yet unmistakably its own.

The band has been described by Rolling Stone as “an eclectic blend of rumbero percussion, delicate organs, and grungy fuzz,” while NPR calls the project “perhaps one of the most unique groups around today.”

Their sound is anchored in the rich rhythmic traditions of Panamá and delivered with the force of a psychedelic rock show. Chi weaves the mejorana, a traditional hand-made instrument rarely heard outside of Panamá, into each performance.

Making Movies is collaborative across genres, working with artists from Rubén Blades to Kevin Morby, and David Hid
title: Making Movies: A live performance of Ámame, Anabel & Lover | Making Movies | TEDxKC

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Quixotic, an immersive performance collective, brings TEDxKC's 2026 theme "Human After All" to life through an electrifying blend of dance, live music, and video projection.

 Quixotic is an internationally recognized immersive performance collective creating bold, visually striking experiences that fuse contemporary dance, cirque, live music, and cutting-edge design. Known for transforming spaces into living worlds, Quixotic blends theatrical storytelling, innovative technology, and emotionally resonant performance to create unforgettable live experiences.

Quixotic is the creative force behind multiple original immersive productions at Faena Theater Miami Beach, including Allura, Sensatia, and Carmen, helping define the theater’s signature live entertainment identity. In addition, Quixotic produces large-scale outdoor and site-responsive experiences such as Dark Forest and Terra Luna, immersive environments that merge nature, light, sound, and movement into multi-sensory journeys.
title: Human After All — breathtaking live performance | Quixotic  | TEDxKC

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Drawing on his journey as a public speaker and coach, Mthabisi Mhlanga explores how confidence is built through action and experience. His talk encourages audiences to take small steps that create evidence of their abilities, build momentum, and strengthen their belief in themselves. Mthabisi Mhlanga is a keynote speaker, public speaking coach, and product leader dedicated to helping people find and own their voice. Born and raised in Zimbabwe, his journey from academic probation in university to the quarterfinals of the World Championship of Public Speaking shaped his core belief that confidence isn't a personality trait, it's built through evidence. Trained as a CPA at KPMG before transitioning into product management in tech, he brings analytical precision to the deeply human work of communication.

Mthabisi has coached founders, executives, and high-performing teams to speak under pressure and lead with presence. His work centers on helping people rewrite the internal narratives t
title: The Real Antidote to Public Speaking Nerves | Mthabisi Mhlanga | TEDxMcMasterU

author: TEDx Talks
description:
A phone call he never expected became the turning point of his life. In this talk, Dominik Blöchlinger shares how saying yes before feeling ready led him from a small Swiss village to leading one of the biggest international projects in his company at just 20 years old. Through his personal story, he explores why growth rarely begins with certainty—and how the biggest opportunities often start with one simple word: yes. Dominik has built his career at the intersection of engineering, leadership, and continuous improvement. Beginning as an electrical installer and automation technician, he developed hands-on expertise in building, testing, and commissioning complex industrial systems before growing into leadership roles.

Today, as Head of Electrical Assembly at Bioengineering AG, he leads a team responsible for delivering large-scale engineering projects from planning through production and final commissioning. Alongside managing quality, cost, and timelines, he is passionate about op
title: The Best Decision I Wasn't Ready For | Dominik Blöchlinger | TEDxHWZ Studio

author: TEDx Talks
description: Speaker and athlete Kelsey Tainsh has faced physical barriers most of us can't imagine. But she believes the most paralyzing barriers aren't the physical ones; they're the ones we build in our heads. This talk is about changing the narrative we tell ourselves, and how doing so can set us free. Kelsey Tainsh, CSP has been through more in her 35 years than most will endure in a lifetime. Successfully overcoming a brain tumor at only 5 years of age, Kelsey went on to be a happy, healthy kid and a champion athlete. 10 years later, at 15, it all came crashing down when the tumor returned followed by a crippling stroke. Her friends had disappeared, her right side didn’t function and she became paralyzed with fear and self doubt.  Despite her significant physical challenges, she worked hard to pull herself up and charged back into life graduating magna cum laude from the University of Florida and going on to work for one of the most recognized companies in the world – The Coca-Cola Company.
title: Everything I never said out loud | Kelsey Tainsh | TEDxUF

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Nepali singer-songwriter and PhD student Ashra Kunwar has found a way to bridge the gap between grief and activism. Through music and conservation research, she shows how pain can be turned into art, and invites the audience to find the roar within.
 Ashra Kunwar from Nepal is a young and relentless Ph.D. Student at the University of Florida, UN Human Rights Delegate speaker from Nepal, Brand Ambassador for the most reputed Governmental Bank of Nepal, Agricultural Development Bank Limited, and a Singer/ Songwriter/ Founder of the rock band Ashra & The Parables. After completing both her Bachelor’s & Master’s in Environmental Science with Research, she is now doing her Ph.D. degree at the University of Florida, being awarded a Full assistantship scholarship.

She is a relentless, goal-oriented person who is willing to go above and beyond on any project related to her expertise. Top 25 selected youth at the US Embassy youth council, amongst 30,000 plus participants, and a civic engageme
title: Art and Activism: What's Your Roar Within? | Ashra Kunwar | TEDxUF

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Karlton Dennis has helped entrepreneurs, business owners, and investors build strong tax strategies. Drawing on his background in financial literacy, he reframes how we think about filing a tax return not as an annual chore, but as a starting point for building lasting wealth Karlton Dennis is a nationally recognized tax strategist, entrepreneur, and educator dedicated to helping business owners and investors build lasting wealth through smart tax planning. As the founder of a leading tax advisory firm, he has guided thousands of entrepreneurs in reducing their tax liabilities legally while scaling their businesses with confidence. Karlton’s passion lies at the intersection of financial literacy and personal freedom—he believes that understanding the tax code is one of the most powerful tools for creating generational wealth.

Through real-world examples and practical strategies, he inspires audiences to think differently about money, ownership, and wealth building. His mission is to
title: The Cost of Not Knowing | Karlton Dennis | TEDxUF

author: TEDx Talks
description: Dr. Nikkia Gumbs challenges the avant-garde of our social lives. Society tells us that finding "the one" is the only way not to die alone. Here, Gumbs argues that friendship is just as life-saving, if not more so, and deserves to be treated as real infrastructure rather than a consolation prize. Nikkia Reneé Gumbs, Ed.D., is an author, speaker, and founder of The House of the Sun, a platform dedicated to grief literacy, nervous system repair, and new forms of belonging. A University of Florida alum and former higher education leader, she has spent more than a decade advancing disability advocacy and wellness design. Her debut book, The Invisible Grief of Adulthood (2025), introduces Spell-Lit™, a new literary form that ritualizes grief and rupture. Through her video series Sun Talks, filmed in her pajamas as a deliberate refusal of respectability politics, she brings humor and candor to taboo subjects like loneliness, burnout, and the fear of dying unseen. This talk was given at a TED
title: What If I Die Alone?: A Love Letter to Every Unwitnessed Soul | Nikkia Gumbs | TEDxUF

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Philip Chang went from a kid taking blurry photos of the stars to a scientist smashing particles at near light speed, joining the CERN team that discovered the Higgs boson in 2012. In this talk he shows how collaboration is what reveals the hidden structure of, well, everything. Dr. Phillip Chang is a particle physicist on a quest to understand the basic substance that makes us—all of us, and everything that surrounds us—so that we may answer the oldest questions: Where do we come from? His fascination began as a child when I read a cartoon science book. It revealed to him that inside atoms were even smaller particles, hidden worlds that most people never see in their daily lives.

That secret motivated him to study Newton’s laws, then calculus. Determined, he pursued physics at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, joining the ATLAS collaboration at CERN. In 2012, he was part of the team that discovered the Higgs boson that allows all of us to exist. Since then, he has also
title: The ultimate dream machine | Philip Chang | TEDxUF

author: TEDx Talks
description:
She wrote a song on her iPhone in 20 minutes, released it, and moved on. Years later, at a moment when she was questioning whether she could keep going as an artist, that same song landed in a Netflix series.
Las Vegas musician and photographer Sonia Barcelona takes the TEDxLasVegas stage for a live performance woven through three lessons from her creative journey: believe in yourself, know where you come from, and keep expressing. Through “Cinnamon Skin,” “Indian Girl,” and “Heart Station,” she shares the real story behind becoming an artist, from imposter syndrome and family roots to grief, creative block, community, and finding her voice again.
For anyone who has ever wondered if their art matters, Sonia’s story is a reminder: you never know where something you create today might lead, who it might reach, or when it might come back and remind you to keep going. Sonia Barcelona is a Las Vegas-based artist, musician, and photographer whose work bridges music, photography, and visual
title: When You Feel Like Giving Up, Keep Creating, Keep Expressing | Sonia Barcelona | TEDxLasVegas

author: TEDx Talks
description: As two young cancer survivors, we learned lessons before 21 that no classroom could ever teach: to celebrate the little things, to practice gratitude in the face of uncertainty, and to never underestimate the power of small acts of kindness. People often ask us, "How are you so positive?" and the answer is simple: the only way to move forward is to find joy in the everyday moments and privileges most people walk right past. Our talk shares how our cancer experiences shape the ways we live and learn, and challenges others to reframe the hardships that build up their "invisible resumes.” We hope to share our perspectives of gratitude, encouraging the audience to celebrate the small things and step up in small ways for others. Amelia Knopp is a junior at the University of Kansas, studying accounting and sociology. At KU, she is a University Scholar, Truman nominee, KU Blood Drives executivemember, and an accounting teaching assistant. Amelia is a loyal KU basketball fan, an avid reader,
title: Celebrating the small things | Amelia Knopp & Luke Karel | TEDxKU

author: TEDx Talks
description: Success is not guaranteed by a degree, a job, or even hard work. This talk explores the three Ps that shape our journey: Purpose, Path, and Perception. It encourages students to define what they want, build a clear direction toward it, develop the right skills, and stay adaptable in a rapidly changing world shaped by AI and technology. Mr. Anand Singh is a distinguished educationist, strategic leader, and academic administrator with over three decades of leadership in higher education and institutional governance. In 1997, he founded the Hanswahini Group of Institutions, transforming access to quality education. He is also the founder of the Surendra Educational Society (1997), Hanswahini Institute of Science & Technology (2004), and Hanswahini Foundation (2014), driving academic excellence, social responsibility, and community empowerment. Since 2016, Mr. Singh has served as the Director of the Centre for Distance and Online Education (CDOE) at Integral University, Lucknow, modernizi
title: Why We Fail: The 3 Ps of Success | Anand Singh | TEDxKLH Bachupally

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Elizabeth Allenberry explores what it means to risk everything to become yourself. Moving from her gender transition in Wyoming to finding safety and community in Las Vegas, she transforms her story into Becoming the Void Walker, a poetic performance about survival, identity, and reclaiming the power to define yourself beyond fear and pain.

Not everyone survives this journey. Not everyone gets the chance to thrive. Through personal storytelling, poetry, and cosmic imagery, Elizabeth explores transgender resilience, unconditional self-love, and the freedom to step fully into who you are becoming. Elizabeth Allen Berry (They/Them) is a multi-dimensional artist & educator. On stage they combine their talents as a spoken word poet, literary artist, and a classically trained violinist to bring an incredibly unique performance. They are a queer, transgender, & neurodivergent. In 2022 they created Cosmic Q Publishing: A micro press specializing in publishing limited edition zines & books fo
title: Becoming the Void Walker: Journey to Unconditional Self-Love | Elizabeth Alllen Berry | TEDxLasVegas

author: TEDx Talks
description: Most students forget what they learned in school by the weekend but can describe every detail of a book they read months ago. Shane argues this is not a coincidence, and that understanding why changes how we learn, what we choose to read, and how much of it actually stays with us. In this talk, he draws on his own experience as a writer and a reader to make the case that stories have always been the most powerful way to learn. Shane is a Grade 8 student at St. Thomas Aquinas in North Vancouver, and a Mensa Canada member since age 5. At just 10 years old, he became a published author of a science fiction novel, ‘Adventures of Ezza the Rover in Space’, and sequels are already in the works. Shane plays tennis, practices taekwondo, swims, and spends his free time reading. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: How stories teach what textbooks can't | Shane Ardehali | TEDxWest Vancouver Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: In this compelling talk, Dr. Brittany Ramsey challenges the prevailing myth that success and leadership are purely mental pursuits driven by pushing through exhaustion. Dr. Ramsey bridges neuroscience and performance to reveal how physical activity boosts vital cognitive proteins, directly enhancing executive function, memory, and stress resilience. By reframing physical discipline not as an aesthetic pursuit, but as vital infrastructure for cognitive clarity and leadership, this talk demonstrates why true sustainable success must engage both the body and the mind. Dr. Brittany Ramsey is a body transformation strategist and Kinesiology Specialist who studies how physical discipline shapes cognitive performance and long-term success. With over a decade of experience coaching and catalyzing success in high-achieving professionals, she examines the link between physiology, stress resilience, and executive function. Her work focuses on sustainable ambition to help leaders build strength t
title: Accelerating Into Who You Were Meant to Be  | Dr. Brittany Ramsey | TEDxU Chicago Illinois

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Most of us have been taught that resilience is a resource we build over time and draw on after difficulty passes. But the moments that demand it most rarely wait for us to be ready: they arrive in the middle of a performance, a competition, or a crisis. In this talk, Diana makes a case for resilience as a live skill — one that cannot wait until the storm passes.
 Diana is a 14-year-old Grade 9 student who has been training in classical and musical theater singing since age 7. She plays the piano, and is an active theater performer with multiple stage productions to her credit. Beyond the performing arts, Diana pursues debate and French classes. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Resilience is a LIVE skill, not just a LIFE skill | Diana Ashnaei | TEDxWest Vancouver Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: The vocabulary for hard times has never been richer. What we are increasingly missing are the stories — ancestral, deep-rooted, centuries-old — that have carried people through difficulty for generations and held entire cultures together. Maya makes the case for why those stories matter, and what we all stand to lose if we don't. Maya is a Grade 11 student enrolled in the IB diploma program. She has a longstanding passion for the arts, including drawing, sketching, and musical theater, and has been performing as a soprano singer since age 9, with productions in both Tehran and Vancouver. With a strong aptitude in math and physics, Maya plans to pursue computer science and robotics. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Why we should carry the stories of our cultures | Maya Pourassad | TEDxWest Vancouver Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Most teens say that they care about the planet. Amy is challenging that caring is not nearly enough. She makes the case that no matter what career you choose, you don't get to opt out of what happens to your own future. This talk looks at what changes once "someone else's problem" stops being an option.
 Amy is a 16-year-old Grade 10 student who has played competitive soccer for eight years. She also trains in Hapkido, where she teaches younger students, and takes part in local beach cleanups. She has a deep love of the outdoors and a strong interest in environmental work and sustainability. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Climate change : the future you can't opt out of | Amy Liu | TEDxWest Vancouver Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
When grown-ups tell a child "let me help," they mean well. But those words can also mean "your turn is over." In this talk, Chloe makes an amusing and surprisingly persuasive case that children don't start out knowing their limits, they learn them from the adults around them. She asks for something small: ten more seconds before adults step in to help. Ten seconds to think, to try, and to figure it out. It might be all a child needs to start believing in themselves.
 Chloe is a six-year-old Grade 1 student, and the youngest of four siblings. She is a competitive figure skater and enjoys reading, helping in the kitchen, and playing outside with her dog. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: How children learn what they can’t do | Chloe Yu | TEDxWest Vancouver Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
A young man once dreamed of becoming “Iron Man,” but the fate led him into the blue world instead. From knowing little about the ocean to understanding how this vast blue realm sustains life on Earth, he now takes the audience on a journey of discovery and responsibility. This talk is an invitation to see the ocean differently and a call to collective action. Join us to explore why protecting this blue world ultimately means protecting ourselves and the future we leave for our kids.
 Hey! My name is Liu Yihan, a master student majoring in Resources and Environment from iEE, TsinghuaSIGS. I love public speaking. This is also my first time stepping onto such a prestigious stage to share my ideas with you! I truly hope you will enjoy my speech about the ocean! This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: From Iron Man Dream to Ocean Voice | Yihan Liu | TEDxTsinghua SIGS

author: TEDx Talks
description: How are our phones affecting not only our thinking but also our behavior? This talk details the hidden element we all should know about the algorithms driving our social media feeds.  Angela Wang is Grade 9 student at CISB who describes herself as extroverted and a major sports fan. In this TEDx talk, she explores how technology  can distract us, and shares the surprising viewpoints that Silicon Valley tech leaders have on the very devices they created. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: The Hidden Rule  | Angela Wang | TEDxCISB Youth

What if the future of global security is decided not on land—but at sea?

Investor and former U.S. Ambassador Erik Bethel explains why maritime security has become one of the defining geopolitical challenges of the 21st century. With 80% of global trade traveling by sea and nearly all internet traffic flowing through undersea cables, the oceans have become critical infrastructure for the global economy.

From autonomous drones and AI-powered defense systems to the strategic competition between the United States and China, Bethel
title: The Future of War Will Be Won at Sea | Erik Bethel | TEDxBoston

The speaker opens talk with a scientific hook "Convergent evolution" in gliding animals (flying squirrels and sugar gliders)  before turning to her own life as a series of converging experiences. Raised in West Africa collecting plants with her father, she trained in Scientific Illustration in London and spent nine years as a freelance illustrator at Kew Gardens. A 2015 visit to the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque in Abu Dhabi, where she was struck by intricate floral (not geometric) patterns, sparked an 8-year self-funded journey to document the Plants of the Quran taking her from Oman's mountains to the deserts of Sharjah, and involving botanists, scholars, Kew, and communities across faiths.

title: Plants of the Quran | Sue Wickison | TEDxUniversity of Leeds
